Macrons

Consonantal i

Consonantal u

Theme

School & learning

academic adjective

of universities and scholarship

also academically, scholarly, academic life, academic work, academic degree

modern

Traupman 298: insigne acadēmicum, academic credit
M-O s.v. class: academic career (cursus acadēmicus); s.v. graduate (gradus acadēmicus)

acadēmicus, acadēmica, acadēmicum

declension

academic, of a university

Classically “of the Academy”, Plato’s school: Cicero’s Acadēmica, and acadēmicus, an Academic philosopher (Lewis & Short). The university sense is modern.

Other words

  • scholasticus, scholastica, scholasticum — of the schools; scholarly, academic (as against public life); (as a noun) a schoolman

    declension · also used · classical · Plin. Ep. 1.24.4: scholasticīs porrō dominīs; Plin. Ep. 2.3.5; Quint. 4.2.92 (Lewis & Short)

    Post-Augustan: of the schools of rhetoric. Pliny uses it of a man who lives for study rather than for the courts, “academic” in that sense, often with a smile (scholasticā lēge, by the rules of the schools, Ep. 2.20.9).

  • doctus, docta, doctum — learned, scholarly

    declension · also used · classical · Traupman 338

    The plain word for a scholar or a scholarly book: vir doctus, a learned man.

Examples

  • Scholasticīs porrō dominīs, ut hic est, sufficit abundē tantum solī, ut relevāre caput, reficere oculōs, reptāre per līmitem ūnamque sēmitam terere omnēsque vīteculās suās nōsse et numerāre arbusculās possint.

    For academic owners like him, just enough land is plenty: enough to rest the head and the eyes, stroll along the boundary, wear down a single path, know every one of their vines and count their little trees.Plin. Ep. 1.24.4

  • Annum sexāgēnsimum excessit et adhūc scholasticus tantum est

    He is past sixty and still nothing but an academicPlin. Ep. 2.3.5

See also university, school year, professor, student.

SourcesLewis & Short: academicus · Lewis & Short: scholasticus · Lewis & Short: doctus
